bug_semantics: The default object.to_json builtin recursively serialized every list element and accessible object member through a static local WriteValue function without a recursion-depth limit, reference-cycle check, or execution-stack guard. An attacker-controlled template can make a ScriptObject refer to itself and pass it to object.to_json; WriteValue then repeatedly retrieves and serializes the same object until an uncatchable StackOverflowException terminates the hosting .NET process.
flaw_origin: PR #533's member commit a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f first added ToJson and its recursive WriteValue implementation in src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs. Both recursive edges, for list elements and object-member values, were introduced without carrying depth or active-path state. The later squash f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1 landed that exact vulnerable file blob on the main history.

GitHub's first-party PR-commit endpoint https://api.github.com/repos/scriban/scriban/pulls/533/commits exposes the eight-member pre-squash chain; member a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f is specifically titled `feat(json-support): Add object.form_json and object.to_json functions #527`. `git show a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f -- src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs` shows the entire ToJson/WriteValue block added against immediate parent 0e777fe3c747e9ac4d774b8513e092ff3054ce34, directly proving the vulnerable function and both unguarded recursive calls are absent from that parent tree. `git rev-parse` gives the identical ObjectFunctions.cs blob 84299c5881c5077e6bfa7cdaa085659d801625c1 at a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f, final PR member 63af24e80597d88289df5f92c6286e10868378ec, and squash f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1, proving the member's code landed unchanged. `git cat-file -p a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f` supplies the parent and the BIC-only human author/committer/message evidence. `git show 760dc21259f3da6a5adbd3148c260e25f1751706` shows the direct fix adding ObjectRecursionLimit enforcement, EnsureSufficientExecutionStack, and reference-identity path tracking, plus cyclic/deep-graph regression cases. `git tag --contains f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1` begins at 5.10.0 and includes vulnerable pre-fix tags through 6.6.0; `git tag --contains 760dc21259f3da6a5adbd3148c260e25f1751706` begins at 7.0.0. The boundary tag commits resolve to 5.10.0=3afac40c6db288e94d728d9c308fc03fbb3c1adb, 6.6.0=b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7, and 7.0.0=25d148a104dd4d679a1a1932442616599e003c2f.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle starts when PR #533 member a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f creates object.to_json and writes the complete unsafe recursive mechanism; later commits merely preserve or adjust surrounding serialization behavior until the dedicated fix. Because the public PR member chain is reconstructable and its ObjectFunctions.cs blob is byte-identical to the squashed landing, the aggregate main-history commit f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1 is not the smallest BIC. A direct diff from a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f's immediate parent shows ToJson/WriteValue did not exist in the parent and was wholly introduced by the BIC. The squash entered release 5.10.0, remained in tags through 6.6.0, and 760dc21259f3da6a5adbd3148c260e25f1751706 directly eliminated the mechanism before the patched 7.0.0 tag. AI attribution is judged only from the decomposed BIC commit object: it has a human author and committer and no AI/co-author/generated trailer, so later commit metadata is irrelevant and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
